angle: Where other tree materials state splitting rules abstractly, this one builds the split search live on a nonlinear drug-dosage story, sweeping every candidate threshold by summed squared residuals until 14.5 emerges as root and then growing the tree under an explicit minimum-node-size stop.
angle_detail: Start with [06:59]–[12:58] to see the threshold sweep and residual accounting that picks the root, then continue to [13:11]–[18:41] for the overfitting warning and the stopping rule. Note the SSR shorthand for summed squared residuals and that the demo minimum of seven stands in for the usual twenty used in practice. It assumes comfort with bias-variance ideas and least squares, and it never covers entropy, classification trees, or forests, so skip it for those topics.
